title_ja: {友達|ともだち}とのチャット

ミカ：ほんと？{助|たす}かる！{六時|ろくじ}のがあるって
リョウ：おっけー。そういえば、ケンも{来|く}るって

text_en:
Mika: What time for tomorrow's film?
Ryo: How about the 10 o'clock showing?
Mika: Ten, huh… I've got my part-time job tomorrow morning…
Ryo: Oh right. The evening showing, then?
Mika: Really? That helps! Apparently there's one at six.
Ryo: OK. Oh, and Ken says he's coming too.
Mika: No way, can't wait!

title_ja: {打|う}ち{合|あ}わせ{日程|にってい}のご{相談|そうだん}

text_en:
To Mr Sato, Midori Planning Co.
Thank you for your continued support. This is Kimura from Hikari Trading.
Regarding the meeting you kindly proposed for next Monday — unfortunately I am out of the office all that day.
I'm very sorry to ask, but would it be possible to arrange Wednesday or Thursday afternoon instead?
I apologise for troubling you when you are busy, and thank you for considering it.

title_ja: 「また{今度|こんど}」の{意味|いみ}
text_ja: {日本|にほん}に{来|き}たばかりのころ、{同僚|どうりょう}に「また{今度|こんど}{飲|の}みに{行|い}きましょう」と{言|い}われて、とてもうれしかった。{私|わたし}はすぐに{手帳|てちょう}を{出|だ}して、「いつにしますか」と{聞|き}いた。{同僚|どうりょう}は{少|すこ}し{困|こま}った{顔|かお}で「そうですね…また{連絡|れんらく}します」と{言|い}った。{連絡|れんらく}は{来|こ}なかった。{今|いま}なら{分|わ}かる。あの「また{今度|こんど}」は{約束|やくそく}ではなく、{会話|かいわ}を{気持|きも}ちよく{終|お}わらせるための{言葉|ことば}だったのだ。{言葉|ことば}の{意味|いみ}だけでなく、{言|い}い{方|かた}や{顔|かお}を{見|み}ることも、{日本語|にほんご}の{勉強|べんきょう}なのだと{思|おも}う。
text_en: When I had just arrived in Japan, a colleague said, 'Let's go for a drink again sometime,' and I was delighted. I pulled out my planner and asked, 'When shall we make it?' My colleague looked a little uncomfortable and said, 'Well… I'll get in touch.' No message ever came. Now I understand. That 'sometime' wasn't a promise — it was a phrase for ending the conversation on a pleasant note. Watching how things are said, and people's faces, is part of learning Japanese too.
